INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES October 3, 2019

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on October 3, 2019,
in Community Room A, located on the 1st floor of City Hall. Commissioner Willie Agee called the
meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Willie Agee, Chair - Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Arrick Turner, Eastside Facilities Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Fernando Meza, District Four

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Patrick made a motion to approve the minutes from August 1, 2019.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Fragoso, Agee and McLemore
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Arrick Turner gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   The Park Maintenance staff is currently working with Inglewood Baseball Fund
  representatives to complete a batting cage and training center at Darby Park. Batting
  cages were approved earlier this year by City Council. The project should be completed
  by late November.
   Graffiti: For the month of August graffiti was removed from 947 sites and 714 in
  September.

  1
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES October 3, 2019

  Arrick Turner also gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   There will be flag football tryouts Saturday for youth ages 13-14 only. The tryouts will be
  held at Champions Field at 12:00 p.m. This program is in conjunction with the Los
  Angeles Rams.
   Supertots is a sports program for youth ages 2 to 5 and is designed to teach youth the
  fundamentals of sports. The classes are held at Darby Park every Saturday and Sunday.
  You can register for the class online at parks.rec@cityofinglewood.org.
   We are preparing for our annual Haunted House at Rogers Park. The Haunted will be
  October 18, 19, 25 and 26 at Rogers Park, from 5-9 p.m.

  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Thomas Uwal is our new Human Services Superintendent. We are excited for the future of
  the Senior Center under his leadership.
   We are in the final process of our paratransit buses. We expect two (2) of them to arrive
  within the next six (6) weeks and two (2) more in the month of November.
   The chess club and the choir are as popular as ever and we have a newly formed Senior
  Advisory Committee.
   The Care Management Team is working hard to make sure that our most vulnerable
  seniors will have a Happy Thanksgiving.
   The Nutrition program is running successfully. The County has advised that we may apply
  for more program funding.

  Commissioner McLemore asked if there is Thanksgiving food drive where can-goods can be
donated. Mr. Devlia stated that a food drive is in discussion.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes gave an update on the following Capital Improvement Projects:
   The Tennis Courts at Edward Vincent Park were recently re-opened. The tennis court
  renovation project cost approximately $750,000.
   We are now working on renovating the restrooms at Edward Vincent and Rogers Parks.
  The RFP for Rogers Park Bathroom renovation has gone out and we expect to present
  that item to you at the November meeting. We’ve elected to have the vault system for the
  restrooms.
   We propose to go to Council mid-November for the resurfacing of the Pools at Edward
  Vincent Park. The resurfacing will cost about $350,000. The work will start around
  February 2020.
   We have ordered the nets for Pickle Ball at North Park.
   The HVAC system and windows at the Willie Agee Playhouse are on the list of upgrades.

  2
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES October 3, 2019

  Commissioner Agee asked if a contractor has been picked for the pool resurfacing. Sabrina
Barnes stated we are in the bidding process. He also stated that he enjoyed the tennis court
reopening. Commissioner Agee asked for a list of ten items that was created based on the original
survey from years prior. Director Barnes stated that the list is in the last agenda packet. The staff
will resend the packet out to the Commissioners. Ms. Barnes reiterated that the air conditioning
was approved for the Willie Agee Playhouse.

Public Comments

  Michael Asfall stated that on Thursday at 5:55 p.m. he received a call from Parks and
Recreation regarding his field time. He stated that all of the prime time hours went to flag football
and tackle football. Mr. Asfall stated that there are Los Angeles Leagues that are getting
preference over Inglewood residents and teams. Ms. Barnes explained the Field permitting
process to the Commission stating during football season all things football take precedence on the
field. The priority for groups receiving field time after football groups is: Inglewood youth groups,
Inglewood adult groups, non-Inglewood youth groups, non-Inglewood adult groups. Inglewood
groups need to have their paperwork in on time and the information submitted needs to reflect a
roster of at least 51% Inglewood residents. Cedric Pinnix, Laura Pinnix, Sheldon Thomas and Mr.
Rueben spoke on behalf of the Spartan’s League. Commissioner Agee stated that Director Barnes
will investigate further. Ms. Barnes offered to meet with Mr. Asfall the next business day.

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioners Patrick thanked everyone for coming out.

The next meeting will be held November 7, 2019 at 6:00 p.m.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:48 p.m.
